intro: Sigma (Σ capital, σ lowercase, and ς at the end of a word) is the 18th letter of the Greek alphabet — but since around 2021 most people searching for "the sigma symbol" mean the "sigma male" internet meme. Here's the twist: the glyph people actually paste for that meme is usually the 🗿 moai emoji, not the Greek letter at all. This page covers all three — the real letter Σ/σ, the moai people use for the meme, and sigma's serious math and science meanings.

sections.label: The Letter
sections.intro: Sigma is the 18th letter of the Greek alphabet. It has one uppercase form and two lowercase forms — σ in the middle or start of a word, and ς only at the very end. Paste whichever one you need.

sections.label: The Meme Glyph
sections.intro: Despite the name, the character people actually paste for the "sigma male" meme is usually the 🗿 moai — its blank, chiseled stone face nails the deadpan "sigma stare" better than any letter. These are the stoic, emotionless faces that carry the joke.

sections.label: Math & Science
sections.intro: The letter's original job. Capital Σ is the summation operator, and the dedicated math glyph ∑ is a near-identical sibling. Lowercase σ marks standard deviation in statistics and shows up across physics constants.
